question: Can a valid full-page image under the encoded-byte limit consume substantial raster memory in the API writer, and is there an active concurrent memory budget that can bound it?

standalone_go_decode.command: temporary Go harness using image/png Encode and image.Decode, run from the BAS API module

reproduction.interpretation: A valid low-entropy image at a plausible long-page size is accepted by the byte-size policy yet expands to about62.5MiB during writer persistence. This is one fixture, not a browser peak or production concurrency measurement.

browser_fixture.operation: launch a disposable local Playwright browser, load a local 1280x12800 solid page, then capture full-page PNG

attempts.html: solid page with a flat-color background
attempts.result: page.setContent timed out before screenshot capture
page.setContent timed out before screenshot capture

browser_fixture.remedy: Simplified page CSS and changed the load condition; both attempts still timed out before capture.
browser_fixture.remaining_limitation: Actual Playwright screenshot dimensions, driver peak PSS and browser-to-API end-to-end cost remain unknown.
browser_fixture.cleanup: The temporary browser was closed in the fixture's finally path, and temporary fixture files were removed by the harness. Managed BAS was not restarted or altered.

resource_budget_review.current_limits: Neither target constrains active or concurrent screenshot decoding.

live_process_sample.qualification: one running shared-host sample with active browser children; not a quiescent idle baseline and not comparable to peak decode PSS

resource_budget_review.decision: Do not select a per-image cap from idle-only targets or this single non-idle process sample. Establish an active/concurrent envelope before fixing a limit.
